title: Sum of Two Bit Strings
statement:
You get two strings a and b, each the binary form of a non-negative integer. Return their sum, also as a binary string.

The inputs have no leading zeros, except the number zero itself, which is "0". Your answer must follow the same rule. The strings can be up to 10 000 bits long, far beyond what fits in a normal number.

examples.why: 11 + 6 = 17. The carry runs through three columns and adds one digit at the front.
Adding zero changes nothing; the strings have different lengths, so line them up from the right.
1 + 1 is 2: write 0 and carry 1 into a new column.

constraints: a and b contain only '0' and '1'
No leading zeros except for "0" itself
hints: Do it the way you add on paper: right to left, one column at a time.
In each column add the two bits (0 if a string has run out) and the carry. The digit to write is the sum mod 2, the new carry is the sum divided by 2.
Keep going while either string has bits left or the carry is 1. Collect digits and reverse once at the end.

explain.intuition:
Ten thousand bits is far past Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so converting to a number and back silently loses bits. Add the way you do on paper instead. Start at the rightmost column with a carry of 0. Each column sums at most three ones: bit from a, bit from b, carry. Write sum % 2 and carry sum >> 1.

Walk two indexes from the right ends, treating a finished string as zeros, and continue while there is a carry left over. Digits come out right to left, so push them into an array and reverse once at the end instead of prepending to a string.
steps: Set i = a.length − 1, j = b.length − 1, carry = 0, and an empty array out.
While i ≥ 0 or j ≥ 0 or carry is 1: let sum = carry, add a[i] if i ≥ 0 and b[j] if j ≥ 0.
Push sum & 1, set carry = sum >> 1, and move both indexes left.
pitfalls: Using parseInt(a, 2) + parseInt(b, 2). It is wrong past 53 bits.
Stopping when both strings run out and dropping the final carry, so "1" + "1" returns "0".
Prepending each digit to a string, which copies the whole string every time: O(n²) for long inputs.

solutions.title: Through a big integer
solutions.idea: Parse both strings as arbitrary-precision integers, add, and print in base 2. Correct, but it hides the column logic interviewers want to see.
solutions.time: O(n) to O(n²) depending on the runtime

solutions.title: Column addition with a carry bit
solutions.idea: Add right to left, one column at a time, carrying into the next column.

followups: Add the two numbers without using + at all, only XOR, AND and shifts. When does the loop stop?
Generalize to any base from 2 to 36.
